description:

PRODUCT GAP (README, re-measured 2026-09-04): 'a Codex seat is wired but was last proven only to reach the API'. Wiring exists: apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts:64-83,116-150 (`codex exec` with the mission on stdin, MCP bearer through `bearer_token_env_var`, `--ignore-user-config`, codex-only env allowlist), moe-up-credentials.ts + moe-up-env.ts (CODEX_HOME / CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN / OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_API_KEY roster), docs/agent-stack-runbook.md 'Codex seats'. The provider is chosen only by the launcher's `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` env; nothing in the browser shows or chooses it.

FEATURE: (a) agent provider per project chosen in the browser: a durable project setting `agentProvider: claude|codex` (plus a per-goal override), written by an operator-only command, read by the wrapper at spawn (the env `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` still wins and is disclosed on Seats). (b) Seats screen shows provider, credential SOURCE (sign-in file vs env var NAME, never a value) and CLI version per seat; when the chosen provider has no credential the launcher's MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING roster renders verbatim. (c) Codex mission parity: mission text, MCP result-size handling (the codex analogue of MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS; paged reads), tool roster, and the work_get_context / work_release path. (d) Proof: a codex planning seat reads the contract and submits a decomposition, and a codex coding seat delivers a node the verifier accepts and the lander commits.

STEP-4 ADVERSARIAL PASS, part 2 of 2 — the two "NOT COVERED" answers, recorded here per the step's own instruction (add to the owning child or comment here; do NOT file an evidence row, global rail 21). Measured at HEAD d5b191be, read-only, no lease held, zero files touched.

=== (c) RESULT-SIZE PARITY: THE MEASUREMENT LANDED, THE REMEDY DID NOT — AND THE REMEDY HAS NO OWNER ON THE BOARD.

What child B's grandchild task-48932bec actually established (completionSummary + agent-spawn-environment.ts:82-93 at HEAD, codex-cli 0.153.4, measured 2026-09-07 on this host):
```
tool_max_output_tokens, max_output_tokens, output_token_limit, tools.max_output_tokens,
model_max_output_tokens   -> ALL rejected as unknown fields under --strict-config
accepted per-server keys  -> startup_timeout_sec, tool_tool_timeout_sec ONLY (duration, never size)
token_budget              -> `codex features list` = under development / false
```
So `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` is claude's lever and is INERT on a codex seat. The absence is asserted POSITIVELY, which is the right shape — agent-spawner.test.ts:1347 `expect(argument).not.toMatch(/max_output_tokens|output_token_limit|token_budget/u)` over the composed argv.

**THE STEP ASKED: "if codex truncates, confirm the FIX landed rather than the measurement merely being recorded." IT DID NOT LAND, AND THE CODE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN WORDS** (agent-spawn-environment.ts:91-93): *"Bounding the result daemon-side is the real remedy and is a change to the SERVED MCP READ SURFACE, not to the spawn surface — a separate row, not a knob to invent here."* **That separate row was never filed.** Board search over every task JSON for `result size` / `result-size` / `bounding the result` / `max_mcp_output` returns 4 rows: task-48932bec (DONE, the measurement), task-ae309e47 and task-df64aa20 (DONE, the wire proof), and this row. **None owns the daemon-side bound.**

**A FIRST-HAND DATA POINT FROM THIS VERY SESSION, which is stronger than the config measurement because it is a real oversized read on the real wire.** My own `moe.get_context` on this row, called with `commentsLimit: 10`, answered **63,766 characters across 518 lines** and my client REFUSED it: *"result … exceeds maximum allowed tokens. Output has been saved to …tool-results\mcp-moe-moe_get_context-*.txt"*. I recovered by reading that file in slices. **The daemon did not bound its own response; a CLIENT-SIDE harness did.** A codex seat has no such harness and, per the measurement above, no size knob — so the same call on a codex seat has nothing standing between it and an oversized result. That is the concrete shape of planningNotes' FOURTH risk ("a truncating seat plans against a partial contract") and it is unmitigated at HEAD.

Mitigation that DOES exist and should be named rather than ignored: the read tools carry caller-side bounds (`commentsLimit`, `commentsMaxChars`, `maxContentChars`, `limit`), so a disciplined caller can stay small. That is a convention, not a fence — it depends on the seat choosing to pass them.

**Disposition per DELIVERY BIAS: follow-up item, not a completion blocker for this row and NOT a new row from this seat.** Owner if taken up: the served MCP read surface (`moe_get_context`), not the spawn surface. Recording it against task-48932bec's finding is the honest home; that row is DONE, so this comment is the record the step asked for.

=== (a)/(b) CREDENTIAL EXPOSURE — CLEAN, WITH ONE ASYMMETRY WORTH NAMING.

The four operator-visible surfaces the step names, traced at HEAD:
1. **spawn argv** — clean, asserted both providers: agent-spawner.test.ts:216 `not.toContain(req.credential)` (claude) and :294 `not.toContain("agent-secret-0001")` (codex), plus :204-206 excluding an operator secret, the store path and every `MOE_` name. The codex bearer rides `-c mcp_servers.moe-next.bearer_token_env_var=MOE_AGENT_MCP_BEARER` (agent-spawner.ts:95) — the NAME, never the value.
2. **/sessions/read** — emits `providerAtStart` and `agentVersionAtStart` (sessions-read.ts:255,261); the file's own header states "the credential digest stays out of the view on purpose".
3. **Seats render** — seat-disclosure.test.tsx:70,83 `not.toContain(CREDENTIAL_VALUE)`; activation-screen.test.tsx:303,306 also checks `title` ATTRIBUTES, which is where a value hides from a text-only assertion.
4. **refusal/receipt text** — activation-read.ts:129-139 `secretValues()` + `scrub()` replace every secret VALUE with `[redacted]` in `reason`, `ref`, `command` and `version` before publishing (:159,160,165,183,221). Not decorative: the docblock records a MEASURED leak it fences — `fatal: env ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<token>` reached the wire verbatim before it. Asserted at daemon-entry-activation-refusals.test.ts:201-215.

**ASYMMETRY (follow-up, not a defect):** `secretValues()` is provider-generic — it calls `providerCredentials(providerFor(agentCommand), …)` and every PRESET credential is built by `secretEntry(...)` with `secret: true`, so the CODEX roster (CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN / OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_API_KEY) is scrubbed by the same code path. But every asserting arm is claude-flavoured (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`). The sign-in branch correctly returns `secret: false` with the login DIRECTORY as its value — a path, not a token. A codex-flavoured redaction arm is the missing coverage; the production behaviour is already correct.

QA REVIEW EVIDENCE — REJECT. All measurements at HEAD `205b1643` (two commits past the `d5b191be` the completion record measured: `25827b94`, `205b1643`, both task-84cd2e55).

## VERDICT: 3 of 5 DoD clauses delivered, 2 open. Reject on DoD 1 (browser half) and DoD 4.

## FINDING 1 — DoD 1's "UI toggle" is not a control, it is a permanently-disabled control that misattributes its own failure. CONFIRMED, not inferred.

The completion record and the channel both stop at `git grep -c set_agent_provider -- affordance-read.ts` -> 0. I traced the consumer to the branch it actually takes in production:
```
live-ops.tsx:181   surface.offers.find((c) => c["commandKind"] === AGENT_PROVIDER_COMMAND_KIND) ?? null
toggle.tsx:56      if (port === null || offer === null || sending.current) return;
toggle.tsx:79      const disabled = port === null || offer === null || busy !== null;
toggle.tsx NOT_OFFERED = "This browser session cannot change the provider. The daemon offers
                          that setting only to a paired operator, so pair this browser and
                          read the seats again."
```
The daemon mints no offer of that kind, so `offer` is null **on every poll, for every session, paired or not**. The toggle is therefore always disabled, under a message that tells a correctly-paired operator to go pair. **An operator who does everything right is told they did it wrong.** That is worse than an absent control, and DoD 1 says "and a UI toggle" while the row title says "chosen in the browser".

`affordance-read.ts:34,36` imports `resolveDeployTargetOffers` and `resolvePlanningOffers`; there is no `affordance-agent-provider-offers.ts` (`ls` -> No such file).

## FINDING 2 — why six green gate legs could not see it. Positive control, run by me:
```
$ npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/http/affordance-read.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  41 passed (41)   Duration 7.51s
```
Green at HEAD **with the offer absent**, because `affordance-read.test.ts` contains **zero** references to `set_agent_provider` (grep: no match) — while 20 test-side references exist at other seams (`daemon-command-registry.test.ts:265,387,404,532-601`, `daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts:227,301`, `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:149-150`, `mcp-main.test.ts:212`). The kind is registered, capability-bound, OPERATOR_ONLY, MCP-excluded, generated into the client, and tested at four seams — **none of which is the one seam that makes it reachable.**

And the browser half tests a fixture: `agent-provider-toggle.test.tsx:37,55,72,114` pass a hand-built `OFFER` constant. The only arm production ever reaches is `:87 offer={null}` — which passes, asserting the refusal copy. **The suite proves the dead branch works.** Global rail 9's set-equality (every served offer advertised, every advertised offer served) has zero coverage at this seam.
